ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

ns1:item.ns1:title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77925-y

In this exploratory randomized trial, the monoclonal antibody AER002 was safe but did not improve clinical or biomarker outcomes in Long COVID. Post-hoc findings suggest baseline antibody levels and drug exposure may inform future studies.
ns1:item.dc:title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial

ns1:item.ns1:title: Stress homogenization enabled by a layered composite electrolyte for high-performance all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78129-0

Mechanical stress limits the lifetime of solid-state lithium metal batteries. Here, authors reveal that the mechanical electrochemical coupling governs battery cycling and develop a layered solid electrolyte that enables uniform lithium deposition and durable solid-state batteries.
ns1:item.dc:title: Stress homogenization enabled by a layered composite electrolyte for high-performance all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
